_说明: Hand-maintained database list. When a name matches, the report shows the type's message as a "database hint". This is not evidence from the paper and does not change the access category. Entries are matched in order and the first match wins (so more specific entries come first). pattern is a regular expression; case_sensitive true means case-sensitive matching (e.g. Wind, to avoid matching wind speed).

paid.message: Commercial database; usually requires payment or an institutional subscription. Ask your university library whether it subscribes

gov_micro.message: Government microdata survey; individual-level data usually require a formal application or are unavailable. Aggregate figures can be found in published statistics

academic_survey.message: Academic survey database; usually requires registration and an application on the official site, and students can generally obtain it. Check that the survey years you need have been released

yearbook.message: Statistical yearbook publications; usually available in libraries or on statistics bureau websites. Check that the years and geographic levels you need are complete (the edition year is usually one year later than the data year)

open_science.message: Data published by research institutions (e.g. NASA, climate models, satellite products); usually free to download from the official site, some require an account

public_disclosure.message: Public disclosure documents (e.g. listed-company annual reports); usually free to download from exchange or disclosure websites, but you need to compile the data yourself

gov_portal.message: Data published by government departments; some can be queried or downloaded on the official site, some require registration or an application. Check the years and levels you need on the department's website

policy_doc.message: Policy documents (lists, implementation dates, guidelines); usually publicly available on government websites, but you need to check and code the variables yourself

gov_public_micro.message: Public-use microdata published by a government statistics agency (e.g. the US CPS): public-use versions are usually free to download from the official site; finer geography or sensitive variables may require a separate restricted version. A survey series has several parts (e.g. ASEC, ORG, the basic monthly survey) with different content and years; check each paper's original name separately
